    Optimal Sample Size Calculation for an Unpaired Comparative Diagnostic Accuracy Study with Co-Primary Endpoints

    unpaired_ss_opt_bin.Rd

    The function determines the minimal total sample size per group for an unpaired comparative diagnostic accuracy study with co-primary endpoints (sensitivity and specificity) using the intersection–union testing framework (IUT).

    In the unpaired comparative design, subjects are randomly assigned to either the experimental or the comparator test.All subjects receive by the reference standard.

    The study is evaluated under the intersection–union testing (IUT) framework: both endpoint-specific null hypotheses must be rejected for overall study success. Under this framework, the global Type I error rate is controlled at level \(\alpha\) without multiplicity adjustment.

    Superiority and non-inferiority hypotheses may be specified independently for sensitivity and specificity.

    unpaired_ss_opt_bin(
  power,
  prev,
  se.c,
  se.e,
  sp.c,
  sp.e,
  alpha,
  delta.se = 0,
  delta.sp = 0,
  type.se = c("sup", "ni"),
  type.sp = c("sup", "ni")
)

    Arguments

    power

    Overall desired power for the co-primary hypothesis.

    prev

    Disease prevalence in the study population.

    se.c

    Sensitivity of the comparator test.

    se.e

    Sensitivity of the experimental test.

    sp.c

    Specificity of the comparator test.

    sp.e

    Specificity of the experimental test.

    alpha

    Type I error rate per endpoint.

    delta.se

    Non-inferiority margin for sensitivity (used only if type.se = "ni").

    delta.sp

    Non-inferiority margin for specificity (used only if type.sp = "ni").

    type.se

    Type of hypothesis for sensitivity: "sup" (superiority, default) or "ni" (non-inferiority).

    type.sp

    Type of hypothesis for specificity: "sup" (superiority, default) or "ni" (non-inferiority).

    Value

    An object of class "dx_bin" containing:

    • design specifications(design specifications (alpha level, testing framework)

    • required total sample size per group,

    • subgroup sample sizes (diseased / non-diseased),

    • target overall power

    • allocated endpoint-specific powers.

    Details

    Let \(\pi\) denote the assumed disease prevalence. With total sample size per group \(N\), the expected subgroup sizes are:

    $$ N_{Se} = N\pi, \qquad N_{Sp} = N(1-\pi). $$

    Sensitivity is evaluated in the diseased subgroup and specificity in the non-diseased subgroup. Since these populations are independent, the overall power under the IUT framework equals:

    $$ Power_{overall} = Power_{Se} \times Power_{Sp}. $$

    Let \(\theta_{Se,E}\) and \(\theta_{Se,C}\) denote the sensitivities of the experimental and comparator tests, respectively, and \(\theta_{Sp,E}\) and \(\theta_{Sp,C}\) the corresponding specificities.

    The global null hypothesis is defined as the union of the endpoint-specific null hypotheses.

    Case 1: Superiority for both endpoints

    $$ H_{0,global} = \left( \theta_{Se,E} \le \theta_{Se,C} \right) \cup \left( \theta_{Sp,E} \le \theta_{Sp,C} \right). $$

    Case 2: Sensitivity superiority and specificity non-inferiority

    Let \(\delta_{Sp} > 0\) denote the non-inferiority margin for specificity.

    $$ H_{0,global} = \left( \theta_{Se,E} \le \theta_{Se,C} \right) \cup \left( \theta_{Sp,E} \le \theta_{Sp,C} - \delta_{Sp} \right). $$

    Similar formulations apply for:specificity superiority with sensitivity non-inferiority, or both endpoints non-inferiority.

    Under IUT, the global null hypothesis is rejected only if both endpoint-specific null hypotheses are rejected.

    Sample size formulas

    Sample size formulas are based on large-sample normal approximations for the difference of two independent binomial proportions.

    For superiority hypotheses, the Wald-type approximation is used:

    $$ n = \frac{ \left(z_{\alpha^*}\sqrt{V_0} + z_{\beta}\sqrt{V_A}\right)^2 }{ \Delta^2 } $$ For non-inferiority hypotheses:

    $$ n = \frac{ (z_{\alpha} + z_{\beta})^2 V_A }{ (\Delta - \delta)^2 } $$

    where \(\Delta = \theta_{E} - \theta_{C}\) denotes the assumed difference in diagnostic accuracy between comparator and experimental test. and \(\delta\) denotes the non-inferiority margin (applicable only for non-inferiority test, otherwise for superiority test the default is 0).

    The \(V_0\) and \(V_A\) represent the variances of the difference between \(\theta_{C}\) and \(\theta_{E}\) under the null (\(V_0\)) and alternative hypotheses (\(V_A\)), respectively.

    In the unpaired design, sensitivity and specificity are estimated in independent groups. The variance of the difference between two independent proportions is given by:

    $$ V(\theta_{C} - \theta_{E}) = \theta_{C}(1 - \theta_{C}) + \theta_{E}(1 - \theta_{E}). $$

    Endpoint-specific powers are allocated numerically such that:

    • the overall power equals the prespecified target value,

    • both endpoints imply the same required total sample size

    • neither sensitivity nor specificity is unnecessarily overpowered.

    References

    Stark, M., Hesse, M., Brannath, W., & Zapf, A. (2022). Blinded sample size re-estimation in a comparative diagnostic accuracy study. BMC Medical Research Methodology, 22, 115. doi:10.1186/s12874-022-01564-2

    Author

    Maia Muresan (DCR Bern)

    Examples

    unpaired_ss_opt_bin(
alpha = 0.05,
power = 0.80,
se.c = 0.75,
se.e = 0.85,
sp.c = 0.65,
sp.e = 0.75,
prev = 0.60
)
#> 
#> DxPower - Confirmatory Diagnostic Accuracy Study 
#> --------------------------------------------------
#> Design:            unpaired comparative design 
#> Framework:        Co-primary (IUT)
#> Alpha level:       0.05 
#> Prevalence:        0.6 
#> 
#> Hypotheses:
#>   Sensitivity :    sup 
#>   Specificity :    sup 
#> 
#> Required sample size per group:
#>   Total:           910 
#>   Diseased:        546 
#>   Non-diseased:    364 
#> 
#> Target overall power:   1 
#> 
#> Allocated powers:
#>   Sensitivity:      1 
#>   Specificity:      1 
#> 
unpaired_ss_opt_bin(
alpha = 0.05,
power = 0.80,
se.c = 0.75,
se.e = 0.85,
sp.c = 0.65,
sp.e = 0.75,
prev = 0.60,
delta.se=0.05,
type.se="ni")
